ORDER APPROVING SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT 

On July 8, 2021, Michigan Gas Utilities Corporation (MGUC) filed an application, along with 
supporting testimony and exhibits, requesting authority to discontinue natural gas services and 
abandon a related natural gas main and distribution line in Calhoun County pursuant to 
MCL 460.6z. 

A prehearing conference was held on September 15, 2021, before Administrative Law Judge 
Jonathan F. Thoits. MGUC and the Commission Staff participated in the proceeding. 
Subsequently, the parties submitted a settlement agreement resolving all issues in the case. 

The Commission has reviewed the settlement agreement and finds that the public interest is 
adequately represented by the parties that entered into the settlement agreement. The Commission 

Page 2 
U-20983 
further finds that the settlement agreement is in the public interest, represents a fair and reasonable 
resolution of the proceeding, and should be approved. 

THEREFORE, IT IS ORDERED that the settlement agreement, attached as Exhibit A, is 
approved. 

The Commission reserves jurisdiction and may issue further orders as necessary. 

Page 3 
U-20983 

Any party desiring to appeal this order must do so in the appropriate court within 30 days after 
issuance and notice of this order, pursuant to MCL 462.26. To comply with the Michigan Rules of 
Court’s requirement to notify the Commission of an appeal, appellants shall send required notices 
to both the Commission’s Executive Secretary and to the Commission’s Legal Counsel. 
Electronic notifications should be sent to the Executive Secretary at mpscedockets@michigan.gov 
and to the Michigan Department of the Attorney General - Public Service Division at 
pungp1@michigan.gov. In lieu of electronic submissions, paper copies of such notifications may 
be sent to the Executive Secretary and the Attorney General - Public Service Division at 7109 
W. Saginaw Hwy., Lansing, MI 48917.

SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT 
Pursuant to MCL 24.278 and Rule 431 of the Michigan Administrative Hearing System’s 
Administrative Rules, R 792.1043, Michigan Gas Utilities Corporation (“MGUC” or the 
“Company”) and the Michigan Public Service Commission (“Commission”) Staff (“Staff”) agree 
as follows: 
1.
On July 8, 2021, MGUC filed an application requesting authority to discontinue
natural gas services and abandon a related natural gas main and distribution line in Calhoun 
County, Michigan. MGUC represents that the natural gas main in question was used to transport 
gas to and from the Mymachod #3-13 storage well and the Partello compressor station/facility. In 
2019, the Company plugged and abandoned Mymachod #3-13 storage well, thereby converting 
same to an observation well and eliminating the need for the transportation of gas by the main line 
in question. There is only one commercial customer that receives natural gas service off the main, 
and this customer uses natural gas on a part-time basis to run a single cylinder engine for a pumping 
unit on an oil well the Mymachod #5-13 and only used 2,530 CCfs of natural gas over the last 12-
month period. MGUC determined that cost for maintaining the line and associated equipment 
outweighs revenue received and advised the customer that the Company intended to abandon the 
EXHIBIT A

2 
line. Subsequently, with the understanding that the Company will contribute towards arrangements 
to be made by the customer to be converted to another energy source, the customer signed a release 
and settlement, a copy of which was attached to the application as Attachment A-2. 
2. 
On August 2, 2021, the Commission’s Executive Secretary issued the Notice of 
Hearing in this proceeding directing the Company to mail and publish the Notice of Hearing. On 
August 30, 2021, the Company electronically filed its affidavit of mailing and proofs of publication 
demonstrating compliance with the Executive Secretary’s noticing directives. 
3. 
On September 15, 2021, Administrative Law Judge Jonathon Thoits conducted a 
prehearing conference. The Company and Staff participated in the proceeding. There were no 
intervenors. 
4. 
The parties have participated in settlement discussions and agree that MGUC’s 
application should be granted and its request to abandon the natural gas main and distribution line 
in Calhoun County, Michigan as set forth in the application, and discontinue natural gas service to 
the customer who signed the release and settlement as submitted with the application should be 
granted. 
5. 
All of the signatories are of the opinion that this settlement agreement is reasonable, 
prudent and will aid in the expeditious conclusion of this case. 
6. 
This settlement agreement is entered into for the sole and express purpose of 
reaching a compromise among the parties. All offers of settlement and discussions relating to 
this settlement are considered privileged under MRE 408. If the Commission approves this 
settlement agreement without modification, neither the parties to the settlement nor the 
Commission shall make any reference to, or use this settlement agreement or the order approving 
it, as a reason, authority, rationale or example for taking any action or position or making any 

3 
subsequent decision in any other case or proceeding; provided, however, such references may be 
made to enforce or implement the provisions of this settlement agreement and the order approving 
it. 
7. 
Pursuant to Rule 431(6) of the Michigan Administrative Hearing System’s 
Administrative Rules, R 792.1043(6) the parties agree any order approving this settlement 
agreement shall not establish precedent for future proceedings and shall not be used as such. This 
settlement agreement is based on the facts and circumstances of this case and is intended as the 
final disposition of Case No. U-20983 only. If the Commission approves this settlement 
agreement, without modification, the undersigned parties agree not to appeal, challenge or 
otherwise contest the Commission order approving this settlement agreement only. 
8. 
This settlement agreement is not severable. Each provision of this settlement 
agreement is dependent upon all other provisions of this settlement agreement. Failure to comply 
with any provision of this settlement agreement constitutes failure to comply with the entire 
settlement agreement. If the Commission rejects or modifies this settlement agreement or any 
provision of this settlement agreement, this settlement agreement shall be deemed to be 
withdrawn, shall not constitute any part of the record in this proceeding or be used for any other 
purpose, and shall not operate to prejudice the pre-negotiation positions of any party. 
9. 
The parties agree to waive Section 81 of the Administrative Procedures Act of 1969 
(MCL 24.281), as it applies to the issues in this proceeding, if the Commission approves this 
settlement agreement without modification.
